description: #3830 — READ-command differential over `get_link_metadata`, waived as "link_metadata cache outside the conformance snapshot scope" until a fixture could put the same rows on both stacks; `seed.link_metadata` is that, inserted verbatim into the backend `link_metadata` table and the mock's map. `get_link_metadata_inner` is `link_metadata::get_cached`: the stored row for a seen url, `None` for an unseen one. The mock answered a hard-coded stub (`title: 'Mock Title'`, `fetched_at: Date.now()`) for ANY url and never `null`, which is the divergence this fixture found and fixed. Two seeded rows discriminate every column: one fully populated with `auth_required: true`, one with every nullable column null and `not_found: true`; `fetched_at` is fixture-authored epoch-ms, not a wall clock, so it is comparable. The flags are booleans on both stacks (the backend struct has `bool` fields; the seed binds them as the 0/1 INTEGERs `upsert` writes), so a mock that stored 0/1 would not agree. NOT pinned: `fetch_link_metadata` (still waived — it goes to the network and upserts, which the mock cannot do).
name: query_link_metadata

queries.comment: The fully populated row: every column comes back as seeded, `auth_required` as the boolean `true`. A stub answer (`Mock Title`, a clock stamp, `auth_required: false`) fails on every attribute but the url.
queries.name: get_link_metadata_hit_populated

queries.comment: The row with every nullable column null and `not_found: true`: a cached negative result is still a HIT, answered with the flag rather than `null`. Discriminates the null columns from the populated row above.
queries.name: get_link_metadata_hit_not_found_row

queries.comment: An unseen url answers `None`, zero rows — not a refusal, and not a stub. The mock answered its fetch stub here, which is the divergence this step found. `expect_empty` says the absence is the point; non-vacuous because the two steps above serve rows through the same command.
queries.name: get_link_metadata_miss_is_none
